title: Here's How One Teacher Humanized Her Online Learning Space with a Story-Driven Intro Video r-online-learning-space-with-a-story-driven-intro-video
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Dave Stuart Jr. highlights an intro video made by Sara G, a Chicago-area English teacher, as a model for humanizing an online learning space at the start of distance learning. He breaks down five specific moves that make her video effective: touching on her childhood, sharing her path into teaching, connecting personally to her subject, revealing interests outside school, and balancing humility with confidence ("humble and bold"). Stuart frames these choices as concrete, replicable techniques rather than abstract advice, arguing that an intro video's power comes from small, human details rather than production polish. He closes by reassuring teachers that their own videos will be effective precisely because they'll be idiosyncratic and personal, not because they match Sara's specific choices.
points: Sara's video succeeds by disclosing small personal details — childhood, path to teaching, love of her subject, life outside school — that humanize her before instruction even begins.
The "humble and bold" balance (acknowledging difficulty while showing unwavering passion) is identified as a key credibility-building move.
Stuart argues effectiveness comes from idiosyncratic, personal choices, not from copying someone else's template or achieving professional polish.
The recommended response to feeling overwhelmed by a strong example is to return to the question, "what would this look like if it were simple?"
quotes: Sara touches on her childhood. Students are fascinated by the places we're from — whether we grew up in the same place we teach or (as in Sara's case) somewhere further away.
Sara shares the path that brought her to teaching. I think most students assume that teachers pop out of the womb fully aware of their fates as future educators.

She touches on her subject. As an English teacher, Sara anticipates that not all of her students will appreciate reading. She acknowledges this while explaining the logical route that brought her to a love of books.

Sara shares her interests outside of school. Her love for her children is obvious in the film, and while Sara's students probably can't relate to the exact idea, they can appreciate that they have things and people that they love, too.

She hits the notes of humble and bold. Again and again, Sara brings it back to teaching — why she loves what she does, why her current role as a distance teacher is difficult, why her passion for her work remains unchanged even in a world wrought with uncertainty.
It's important to remember that videos like this are going to be as idiosyncratic as the people who make them. When we look at examples of good teaching, we need to monitor our insides.
